clue.text: Girl's piano arrangement for A Shropshire Lad?

parts.note: Sal is a short girl's name, Sally

indicators.note: an arrangement of the word piano puts its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A girl has arranged a piano piece to accompany Housman's poem A Shropshire Lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' gives OPIAN. The surface points to Housman's poem cycle, but the question mark marks a cryptic definition: any lad from Shropshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Salop is an old name for the county of Shropshire, so a native of it is called by the demonym derived from that name.

clue.text: Has meal with drink on board ship, showing sea legs?

indicators.note: on board means the other pieces are put inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
tea is a drink
dines means has a meal

explanation.surface: Eating and drinking on a ship shows that one has found one's sea legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the container signal: a ship's letters hold the drink and the meal. 'sea legs' is a noun phrase, matching the noun answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Having sea legs means keeping balance on a moving ship, which is stability or firmness.

clue.text: Leading aircraftman revealed source of varnish

definitions.meaning: a resin secreted by insects, from which shellac is made

explanation.definitionFit: The letters are the RAF abbreviation for leading aircraftman and also the insect resin used to make shellac varnish.

clue.text: A hobo surprisingly admitted by pressure on hospital official

indicators.note: admitted by means taken in between the letters for pressure and hospital

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the words a hobo are oddly rearranged

explanation.surface: A tramp is unexpectedly let into hospital because of pressure from an official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges A HOBO into OOHBA, which 'admitted by' puts between P and H.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Lord High Everything Else in The Mikado, the name means a pompous official holding many offices.

clue.text: Tough subject retaken in GCE arrangement

indicators.note: arrangement says the letters of the words retaken in GCE are reordered

explanation.surface: A difficult subject is retaken in a GCE exam arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: GCE is the old British school examination, the General Certificate of Education, which fits the surface of a resit.
explanation.definitionFit: The classical language of Homer and Plato is a famously hard school subject.

clue.text: Bishop setting standard in English church

indicators.note: in places the standard inside the pair of abbreviations for English and church

parts.note: par is a standard or norm, as in 'up to par'

explanation.surface: A bishop sets the standard for the English church.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Eastern Orthodox church a senior bishop, the head of an eparchy, holds this title.

clue.text: Nobles always protected by servant

indicators.note: protected by means surrounded by the servant's letters

parts.note: a page is a young servant
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Noblemen are always guarded by a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: E'er, the poetic contraction, is a common crossword source for these three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the body of nobles collectively, the lords of the realm.

clue.text: Just the Conservatives raised an objection

parts.note: the right is the political wing of the Conservatives
minded means objected, as in 'did you mind?'

explanation.surface: The Conservatives merely raised an objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like the adverb 'merely'; it is the adjective 'fair'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone just is fair and morally sound in judgement, having sound principles.

clue.text: Search for shelter round base of mountain

indicators.note: round means the shelter goes around the next letter

parts.note: a hut is a simple shelter

indicators.note: base of a down clue's word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A search for shelter takes place around the foot of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts N, the last letter of mountain, inside HUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To hunt for something is to search diligently for it.

clue.text: Go too far in foreign carriage, crossing river

parts.note: en is French for in, so 'in' in a foreign language

indicators.note: the carriage crosses, or straddles, the letter for river, which sits inside it

parts.note: a coach is a horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Someone travelling abroad in a carriage goes too far when crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' makes CROACH; 'foreign' signals a French word for 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to intrude beyond proper limits, overstepping the line into another's territory.

clue.text: Port imbibed by sober gentlemen

indicators.note: imbibed by says the port is drunk down inside the words sober gentlemen, its letters running across them

explanation.surface: Sober gentlemen nonetheless drink port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink being imbibed; it is the Norwegian seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergen is a major seaport on the west coast of Norway.

clue.text: One can barely crawl

parts.note: barely means naked, and crawl is the swimming stroke, so this is someone swimming without clothes

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who swims naked can do the crawl stroke only in the bare sense.

clue.text: Terriers, for example, taking meal in mess

parts.note: terriers are one example of dogs
breakfast is a meal

explanation.surface: Terriers make a mess while eating their meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an untidy muddle or botched job is a British colloquialism for a mess.

clue.text: Sharing novel haggis out

indicators.note: out signals the words novel and haggis set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A new haggis is shared out among the diners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the adjective describing the haggis; it is fodder with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting something equally between two is the idiom for sharing it.

clue.text: Complaint of experienced hikers and beginners

definitions.meaning: sore feet that hurt after long walking
novices, plural of a word for a newcomer or greenhorn

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is sore feet; as the plural of an Americanism it means novices or greenhorns.

clue.text: What nag is heard to say at start of Australian soap

definitions.text: What nag is heard to say

indicators.note: at the start of says only the opening part of the soap's title is used, the rest dropped

parts.note: Neighbours is a long-running Australian TV soap opera, widely shown in Britain

explanation.surface: A horse whinnies at the opening of an Australian soap opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first five letters of NEIGHBOURS are kept, dropping BOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the cry a horse makes, and nag is a slang word for an old horse.

clue.text: Taste before gathering in fruit

parts.note: a tang is a sharp taste

indicators.note: gathering means the word for before takes in the word in

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
taken as written

explanation.surface: A taste comes before gathering in the fruit harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like it is placing the taste first; it supplies ERE, which 'gathering' wraps round IN to make ERINE.
explanation.definitionFit: This small loose-skinned orange-red citrus is a kind of mandarin.

clue.text: Cheese: is it wise before a race?

indicators.note: before places wise ahead of race

parts.note: sage means wise
the Derby is a famous horse race run at Epsom

explanation.surface: A cheese wonders whether it is wise before running a race.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an English cheese flavoured and marbled green with sage leaves, from Derbyshire.

clue.text: Digger, briefly upset, is given single drug

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the shortened word upside down
briefly means the word for digger is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a spade is a digging tool
one means single

explanation.surface: A digger, briefly upset, is given a single drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter, leaving SPAD, and 'upset' turns that to DAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dapsone is an antibacterial medicine used chiefly to treat leprosy.

clue.text: So cryptic, clues often defy expert deconstruction at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: Cryptic clues often defy even an expert's attempt to take them apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coded is written in cipher, hidden and hard to read, which is to be cryptic.

clue.text: Many ways to present pieces of toast

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
routes are ways to go

explanation.surface: There are many ways to serve pieces of toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Croutes are small slices of toast or fried bread used as a base for savouries.

clue.text: Request for dessert quite unlike 12

definitions.meaning: read literally, an order for apple pie in a restaurant
the phrase means perfect neatness, the opposite of a mess

explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is a mess, so its opposite is perfect tidiness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes everything neatly arranged, the reverse of a muddle.

clue.text: Friend supplied fish

definitions.meaning: chopped fish thrown in the water as bait

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a close friend and also chopped fish scattered as bait for anglers.

clue.text: Wear kid

definitions.meaning: to be dressed in, as in a coat one has on
to tease or fool someone, British slang

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to be dressed in clothes and, in British slang, to tease or deceive.

clue.text: Fierce-tempered person displayed grudge, having to carry wood

indicators.note: having to carry says the grudge holds the wood inside it

parts.note: spite is a malicious grudge
fir is a timber wood

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered person shows a grudge while having to carry wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' is only a link word; 'grudge' alone supplies the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a fiery, quick temper is colloquially called by the name of something that spits flame.

clue.text: I oddly recognised former president

annotationWithheld.why: I oddly recognised former president (3), IKE: no parse found; odd letters of 'I recognised' give IEONSD, not IKE, and no reading of 'recognised' supplies KE

clue.text: Failed to catch film being broadcast

indicators.note: being broadcast means the word is said out loud and heard

parts.note: a film is a thin layer or haze, as is mist

explanation.surface: Someone failed to catch a film that was being shown on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie; it is a thin haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Having failed to catch a ball or a train, one has let it go by.

clue.text: Chance of success in search for gold

definitions.meaning: to explore ground looking for gold or minerals

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means likelihood of success, and the verb means to explore for gold as a miner.
